caseStudy.headline: Cybriila
caseStudy.subhead: SEBI-licensed RTA offering end-to-end mutual fund APIs.
caseStudy.problem: Grow revenue by onboarding new customers and getting them to scale their monthly transaction volume.
caseStudy.challenge: Carve out a clear position in a crowded field against players like BSE, NSE, and MFU and become the default choice for new-age fintechs.
caseStudy.solution: We couldn't out-build the giants, so we didn't try to. We picked one or two things we could do better than anyone and went deep. Fintechs want speed. They want to test a prototype in weeks, not months. So that became our core promise: distribute mutual funds in 3 weeks. The second: fully managed daily ops, because no fintech wants to run day-to-day operations. Then we made sure the sales team carried that exact message to exactly the right customers.

results.value: We grew from ~12 customers in April '22 to over 160 by April '26, including BharatPe, Bachatt, Jar, and Stable Money. Today, Cybrilla processes over 6M transactions a month.

caseStudy.headline: MFStack
caseStudy.subhead: A software development agency that later launched its own product.
caseStudy.problem: Strong technical work, but deals kept slipping to competitors and lead inflow was inconsistent. The capability was there, the edge wasn't landing with buyers.
caseStudy.challenge: Find the positioning and the right ICP that would make their strength legible to prospects, and turn that clarity into closed deals.
caseStudy.solution: Working closely with their team, we mapped what they were genuinely better at than the competition and what they weren't. I built the positioning around that honest read, then translated it into a sales narrative the team could carry into every conversation. We rebuilt the script around the new story and tracked how conversations changed over the following months.

results.value: With a sharper story, they started winning deals they hadn't before including first-of-their-kind engagements like corporate treasury management. One of those builds became the base-layer stack that later grew into MFStack, their own white-labeled app for MFDs and RIAs. The positioning didn't just close deals. It surfaced a product.

caseStudy.headline: Perccent
caseStudy.subhead: A digital B2C mutual fund distribution platform with a human in the loop.
caseStudy.problem: A poor activation-to-investment ratio on the platform. People signed up. Far fewer invested.
caseStudy.challenge: The platform was targeting low-income users, who are mostly cash-strapped, so roughly 40% of incoming leads were really looking for a short-term personal loan, not a place to invest. The task was to find a target audience with actual surplus to put to work.
caseStudy.solution: I spent over two months with the founders, digging into the numbers to understand what was really happening. With a CAC north of ₹2,000 and 72% attrition inside the first 40 days, the company was burning cash fast. We ran a SWOT analysis to find a defensible position in a crowded market and built a pivot plan around it. Two things stood out, a real human in the investment journey was highly valuable to users, and the founders with 20+ years of experience each, had a strong distribution network of their own. Targeting those users in phase one made obvious sense.

results.value: Perccent has over 13,000 registered users today, most earning above ₹25 lakh a year. The average investment ticket is up 20x. And first-30-day attrition, once 72%, now sits under 20%.

caseStudy.headline: FinArk
caseStudy.subhead: A performance data provider for mutual funds.
caseStudy.problem: Almost no conversion from the free tier to paid.
caseStudy.challenge: Investors were comparing FinArk's features and credibility against established names like Morningstar and Value Research. Some businesses started the trial but never converted to paying users.
caseStudy.solution: I was honest about the starting point, a 0-to-1 startup can't match incumbents on feature parity from day one and with data, there's little room to differentiate on the offering itself, since the source, format, and presentation are largely standardised. So we took the two positions that were actually ours to take, better uptime and a clear cost advantage. From there, I reworked the sales script to handle the feature and credibility objections head-on, and recommended old-school, direct demand channels, cold calling and partnership-led funnels to build a pipeline.

results.value: FinArk converted every 1 in 3 trial users in the first three months of running this.
